record.file_problem: Only the README and file list are provided; the listed results.txt file is not included, so its contents cannot be checked.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports harmful-versus-harmless activation differences and an ablation result on Gemma-2B-IT, a direct test of the refusal-direction removal method, though only at a selected layer and position.
record.gate_note: The README reports one ablation outcome. The best-target selection (layer 10, position -1) is not a separate result row. The listed results.txt is unavailable and contributes no extractable findings.
record.test_reason: The repository replicates the original difference-in-means method on Gemma-2B-IT. It uses harmful prompts from LLM-attacks and harmless prompts from Alpaca, ablates the direction, and reports the refusal-score (log-odds) change. That is the original's method and measure.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README reports that the best ablation target was layer 10, position -1, and that ablation moves the refusal score from 5.83 to -13.80, switching Gemma-2B-IT from strong refusal to strong compliance. It says layer 10 had the largest effect among about 18 layers. It frames this as fitting mid-to-late integration of refusal signals.
record.recipe_differences: Replication-style repository (as named); it reports ablation at the selected layer and position rather than projection at every layer and position. No addition or general-capability result is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: The README identifies layer 10, position -1 as the best ablation target and says layer 10 had the largest effect.
record.problems: The supplied text reports only a selected layer-position result; it gives no uncertainty, control, or general-capability result. The underlying results.txt is unavailable.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results could be extracted. The file list names results.txt, but its contents were not provided.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the harmful-versus-harmless activation-difference direction at the selected layer and position.
rows.note: The README describes the change as switching from strong refusal to strong compliance. It reports the selected layer-position result, not an all-layer-and-position ablation.
rows.check: The value comes from the selection step: the best of a layer×position sweep chosen to minimize refusal score. It is an optimistic in-sample number, not a held-out evaluation of generations. The README also says position -1 was 'chosen because last token', which conflicts with the sweep description. It does not say whether ablation was applied only at layer 10 or across all layers, so the condition 'layer 10' may describe where the direction was extracted rather than where it was ablated. No uncertainty is given and the prompt counts are not stated.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2B-IT, direction from layer 10, position -1, selection-set refusal score
relationships.reason: Ablation drops refusal log-odds from 5.83 to -13.80, described as strong refusal to strong compliance (R1). This is the selection-optimized metric only, with no held-out or capability check.
relationships.display_finding: Ablation reduced refusal log-odds from 5.83 to −13.80 on the data used to select the direction.
